readMe:
THIS FILE IS STEP 1 OF tools/loop/ITERATION-PROMPT.md AND IT MUST STAY READABLE IN ONE Read.
STEP 1 READS THREE FILES, NOT ONE: this file, GATES.md, and PLAN.md §14. All three go through a Read
that has TWO ceilings: it TRUNCATES past 25,000 tokens and FAILS OUTRIGHT past 256 KB. BOTH HAVE
ALREADY BITTEN THIS FILE. iter127 hit the byte ceiling - the Read was refused, 459 KB, because the
`done` log had reached 397 KB of it. iter128 found the TOKEN cap had been truncating for longer and
unnoticed: at 74,115 bytes / 31,303 tokens, step 1 returned lines 1-43 of 92 and dropped `decisions`
(the six outstanding decisions), `doneCount`, `doneArchive`, `doneRecent` and `spikes`.

TRUNCATION IS NOT SILENT (corrected iter129): the tool prints an explicit "[Truncated: PARTIAL view - showing lines 1-462 of 1500 total ...]" notice, so the risk is an agent SKIMMING PAST it, not the tool hiding anything. How the B/tok constants were derived from that notice moved to method-notes.md at iter160; check_calibration owns them now.

RUN `python3 tools/loop/check-state-size.py` AFTER EVERY EDIT TO THIS FILE, TO GATES.md, OR TO PLAN.md.
It measures ALL THREE step-1 files (iter128's version measured only this one), prints each file's
HEADROOM IN KB before it truncates, distinguishes the two ceilings, lists this file's largest fields,
flags every other tools/loop file, and EXITS NON-ZERO when something stops fitting.
WHEN IT TRIPS ON THIS FILE: move an append-heavy field into an archive under tools/loop/ and leave a
short pointer behind. There are EIGHT precedents - `doneArchive`, `blockersArchive`, `gatesArchive`,
`methodNotes`, `scratchInventory`, `spikesArchive`, `decisions._archive` (iter130, the one that
keeps its pointer INSIDE the field it drained rather than as a sibling key), and `doneRecent`
(iter151, drained to empty because every entry was already in done-archive.jsonl - see
`doneRecentNote`, and do not refill it) - and each one asserted
its round-trip before this file was rewritten. Do not discard content to make the check pass. WHEN IT TRIPS ON GATES.md OR
PLAN.md: that content is the spec and the gate instructions, so archive a settled section, never drop
one.

AND NOTE WHY THIS PARAGRAPH IS AT THE TOP OF THE FILE RATHER THAN NEXT TO `doneArchive`: a truncated
Read still shows it. iter127's rotation rule was correct and had no effect, because it was written
into a field that sat past the cut. A rule that keeps a file readable is worthless in the half that
gets cut off.
phase:
M6 feature-complete. **ITER166 PAIRED THE ONE STUB LAYER ITERS 159-161 MISSED — method-notes.md's — AND FOUND IT SOUND; THE REAL FINDING WAS IN THE PROBE, WHICH FABRICATED 18 FINDINGS BEFORE IT FOUND ZERO.** Long account: done-archive.jsonl line 167.

  24 of method-notes.md's 26 sections claim "MOVED to `<archive>` at iterNNN, verbatim and round-trip asserted", and **nothing had ever re-checked one**: `check_read_whole_files` asserts the archive FILES exist, which says nothing about whether a stub's section is still in the file it names. Same split iters 159/160/161 closed three times inside state.json; this instance lives in a DOCUMENT, so the enumeration scoped to state.json never reached it. **24/24 resolve, both directions — a green measurement, not a find.**

  **THE PROBE IS THE LESSON. A REGEX THAT UNDER-MATCHES DOES NOT MISS FINDINGS, IT FABRICATES THEM.** `[Mm]oved` does not match the all-caps `**MOVED to`: 18 stubs became "live bodies" and their good archived bodies reported as 18 ORPHAN BODY findings — confident, specific, wrong. The fix still missed `MOVED ON to`, the one section rotated twice. Both caught by an INDEPENDENT count of the same population, not by reading; a vacuity refusal cannot catch this, because it fires on zero and stays silent on 6-of-24.

  Shipped `check_method_notes_stubs` (check #9), **7/7 both ways**, four directions plus an APPENDING refusal — including the direction that cost those two regexes: **a stub-shaped section whose provenance does not parse is a FAILURE, not a live body.**

  Verified: build 0/0; run-suite **1390/1390 skipped=0** before and after; checker exit 0 on nine checks; run-all.py **6/6**. **Nothing was decided, no gate moved, and no check fires on the event the loop is waiting for.**
nextAction:
**RUN `dotnet build` AND `python3 tools/loop/run-suite.py` BEFORE YOU CHANGE ANYTHING AND AGAIN AFTER YOUR LAST WRITE - NOT `dotnet test | tail`**, which keeps the summary and drops the failure lines above it (iter154). **Expect 1390 tests; run-suite.py ENFORCES THAT ITSELF** (`EXPECTED_AT_LEAST`, plus red on an unparseable summary or any skip), so if it reds on a count, read the reason before assuming a test broke: a DROP is the signal, and a deliberate one means editing that constant in the same commit and saying why. Several tests sweep the tree's own PROSE outside `tests/`/`tools/`, so a docs-only edit - GATES.md included - can turn it red. **`dotnet test --nologo` RUNS ZERO TESTS AND EXITS 1**; one class is `--filter-query '/*/*/<Class>/*'`, ONE pattern only (iter143).

**FIRST, RUN `git diff tools/loop/state.json` AND `git status`. AN ANSWER FROM MIRKO ARRIVES AS AN UNCOMMITTED EDIT TO THIS FILE** - that is how iter155 found `decisions.formatOnEditHook`. **Trust `decisions`/`gates` plus GATES.md's checkboxes over any prose in `phase`/`nextAction`**, which are written an iteration earlier.

**`python3 .mtk/paths-163/run-all.py` (now 6/6, ~3 min) IS STILL THE ONE COMMAND THAT RE-CHECKS EVERYTHING ITERS 162-166 TOUCHED** (35/35 cells, 25/25, 5/5, iter166's 7/7, the refusal-appends probe, live checker exit 0). **THE CHECKER SEAM IS SPENT AND SO IS THE STUB-PAIRING ONE. DO NOT RE-PROBE:** claim-dimensions (157-158); sibling instances (159-161); container-vs-body enumeration (161); the soft-flag sweep (162-163); the four PROSE vacuity judgements (164); the four DECLARED refusals and the return-vs-append defect (165); **method-notes.md's stub/body pairing (166, 24/24 sound - the last unpaired stub layer in the tree).**

**THE STANDING BUDGET REMEDY CHANGED AT ITER166 - READ THIS BEFORE YOU ROTATE ANYTHING.** "Condense the stub layer", which this field named for two iterations, is **MEASURED AND WITHDRAWN**: of the stub layer's 26,556 B only **1,829 B is repeated phrasing** (`.mtk/paths-166/measure-stub-boilerplate.py`), so stripping all of it nets ~1.1 KB - less than the section documenting the work - and the other ~24.7 KB is headline CONTENT that cannot go without discarding lessons. **The stub layer is the read path, not the fat.** What DOES pay: rotate the oldest settled `##` section into **`tools/loop/method-notes-archive-3.md`, the CURRENT generation (opened iter166)**. Generations 1 and 2 are FULL AND FROZEN - gen2 is 54 KB / ~22.5 K tok, past the band and inside the Read cap, so rotating there relocates the truncation. Recipe: `.mtk/paths-162/rotate-method-notes.py`, with `.mtk/paths-166/rotate-iter166.py` as the one-section form that shows how to retarget it at a new generation. **A generation 4 must be declared in BOTH `ARCHIVE_FILES` and `METHOD_NOTES_GENERATIONS` in the same change - that is now a FAILING CHECK, not advice.** Do not discard content to make the check pass.

**READ THIS BEFORE INVENTING ANYTHING ELSE: EVERY REMAINING PLAN.md §15 ITEM IS GATED ON MIRKO, AND HAS BEEN FOR ~50 ITERATIONS.** M6 is feature-complete; ten boxes and seven decisions are his. **If you cannot name a specific half-edit that ships green today, prefer re-running an existing harness against HEAD and recording that nothing independent is left.**

**check-state-size.py NOW RUNS NINE CHECKS** and six refuse a vacuous pass explicitly. **THREE DECLARED LISTS MUST BE EDITED IN THE SAME CHANGE AS THE THING THEY DECLARE:** `GATES_ARCHIVE_NON_GATE_KEYS`, `ARCHIVE_FILES` and `METHOD_NOTES_GENERATIONS`. None is inferred from a name shape, deliberately. **SETTLING A BLOCKER IS A FOUR-PLACE EDIT** (iter160) and the fourth - append the body to blockers-archive.jsonl - is the only one whose omission DESTROYS text; iter155 skipped it. **ROTATING A METHOD NOTE IS A THREE-PLACE EDIT** (iter166): body into the current generation VERBATIM, round trip asserted BEFORE the destructive write, stub left behind with heading + destination + headlines. **A REFUSAL APPENDS, IT NEVER `return`s** (iter165) - keep that shape in anything you add.

**MIND THE CEILINGS. state.json: ~45 KB against a 46,000 B budget, so ~1 KB of headroom** - budget your `phase`/`nextAction` against it, and `readMe` (2,538 B) is the next real payback if you need kilobytes. **method-notes.md: 45,004 B, ~3.0 KB of headroom - YOUR OWN SECTION WILL CONSUME MOST OF IT, so rotate iter166's section out as your payback.** gen3 is 8.2 KB and has room.

**THEN CHECK GATES.md. TEN BOXES ARE UNCHECKED AND ALL TEN ARE MIRKO'S** - five milestone gates, five side items, each mirrored one-for-one in `gates`; **check-state-size.py FAILS ON MIRROR OR STATUS DRIFT**, so trust the checker over prose. Cheapest first: restart-loop-driver (three commands, nothing pending), gate-m3 (one `approved` label), gate-m4 (one wrong comment), gate-m5 (answer decisions.m5Acceptance), gate-m2 (walk the 44 pages), gate-m6 (push main, tag v0.1.0). **SEVEN DECISIONS ARE OPEN, ALL MIRKO'S, ALL FULLY MEASURED - DO NOT REDO THAT WORK.** Every embedded *check / find out / see whether* is answered; what is left in each is a JUDGEMENT the loop must not make. Probes: `.mtk/paths-156/`, `-157/`, `-158/`.

**paste-format-on-edit-hook IS A PURE PASTE, ITS QUESTION IS SETTLED - DO NOT RE-ASK IT, DO NOT RECREATE `tools/hooks/format-on-edit.py`.** **The loop cannot write `.claude/`** (path-based classifier above the permission layer); do not retry, do not route around it with an allowlisted `python3`. **tools/loop/docume-loop.sh IS THE ONE FILE AN ITERATION CAN EDIT BUT CANNOT MAKE TAKE EFFECT** - bash parses a `while` loop once and the driver started 2026-07-24, so a 'fix' is probably already committed and merely not running (`gates.restart-loop-driver`; iter140 tested it 9/9 and NO CODE CHANGE IS PENDING). Live because they are re-read by path every pass: ITERATION-PROMPT.md, loop-settings.json.

**MUTATION-HARNESS RULES LIVE IN tools/loop/method-notes.md** (`methodNotes.appendHere`) - read it whole before writing a harness; a plain Read returns all of it. iter166 added five notes there. The two that shaped its own work: **an enumeration keyed on a phrase must be checked against an INDEPENDENT count of the same population before its findings are believed** (a partial match is worse than no match - a vacuity refusal fires on zero and stays silent on 6-of-24), and **when a cell mutates a script, assert the anchor matched EXACTLY ONCE** - iter166's own second rotation made a previously unique anchor ambiguous and the assertion caught it mid-iteration.

**HYGIENE, NOT URGENT, AND DO NOT DELETE IT WITHOUT ASKING** (it is a data file, so the global rule says ask): untracked `tests/golden/.claude/analytics.json`, written 2026-07-24 20:31 by an MTK analytics call whose cwd was `tests/golden`. Harmless today - the suite is 1390/1390 with it present and the prose sweeps exclude `tests/` - but `tests/golden/` is a rule §4.3 contract directory, so a stray `.claude/` in it is a trap for a future golden enumerator. Ask Mirko: delete or gitignore?

blockers._archive: FULL BLOCKER BODIES ARE IN tools/loop/blockers-open.json (moved at iter139; nothing discarded, round-trip asserted — the eighth archive precedent, and like decisions._archive the pointer stays INSIDE the field it drained). Each line below is ONE OPEN blocker: what it is, whose call it is, and where to answer. EVERY ONE IS PHRASED AS A QUESTION FOR MIRKO and every one is also written up at length in GATES.md, which step 1 reads anyway — so open the archive only to ACT on one. NOTE: tools/loop/blockers-archive.jsonl is a DIFFERENT file holding SETTLED blockers. **`blockers` IS AN OBJECT, NOT AN ARRAY** (matching `gates` and `decisions`; nothing reads it programmatically — checked). TO ADD ONE, per protocol step 9: a short kebab-case key here with a ONE-LINE stub ending in a pointer, and the full body in blockers-open.json under the same key. TO SETTLE ONE, **FOUR PLACES, AND check-state-size.py NOW FAILS ON A HALF-EDIT**: delete the key from both, append a one-line verdict to blockersArchive.settled, AND append the body to blockers-archive.jsonl (line shape: `blockersArchive.format`). **THE FOURTH DESTROYS CONTENT IF SKIPPED** - iter155 skipped it. (Condensed iter150 as budget payback; the historical justification for the iter139 move is in blockers-open.json and the done archive.)

Blocks the remote half of gate-m5 and makes gate-m6's tag step misleading; blocks no offline work. Body: tools/loop/blockers-open.json.

It scopes the force-push exception you already authorised (decisions.compositeAction: floating-v1) so a future iteration cannot read §8.2 literally and delete that work. Fix is the committed PreToolUse hook tools/loop/hooks/deny-history-rewrite.py, 25/25, and PROVEN TO LOAD AND FIRE FROM A --settings FILE at iter131, 3/3, without installing anything. **CONFIRMED ITER139: needs NO driver restart** — the running driver re-reads loop-settings.json by path every pass. (b) `Write(.env)` / `Write(.env.*)` in your GLOBAL settings enforce NOTHING — only `Edit(path)` rules are matched for file permissions. gates.gate-m3-approval-roundtrip: PENDING, MIRKO'S, and the cheapest of the five: add ONE `approved` label to any published page ('CLI Reference', id 451969089, is a good one), then tick. The loop then runs `sync --labels`, republishes that page with `publish --notify-reviewers`, and you re-approve. `approvedBy` will read 'unknown' and that is correct, not a bug (spike S3: Confluence exposes no label author). THIS GATE ALSO GATES SHIPPED CODE - iter122's `--notify-reviewers` fires only where a run revokes an approval, and no DOCUMESBX page carries one, so nothing can exercise it live until this box moves.
gates.gate-m4-feedback-roundtrip: PENDING, MIRKO'S. Write ONE comment saying something factually wrong about a published page (an INLINE comment on a sentence exercises the most code), then tick. The loop then runs `sync --comments` -> `/docs-feedback` -> a `docs/feedback-<date>` PR -> republish -> `sync --reply`.
gates.gate-m5-refresh-roundtrip: PENDING, MIRKO'S, and it is a DECISION not a task: does M5's §14 acceptance run on this repo (copy docs-drift-pr.yml in, add secrets) or fold into M7 where a real repo with real PRs exists? Answer in decisions.m5Acceptance. gates.gate-m6-first-release: PENDING, MIRKO'S, and the only irreversible one - a package on a GitHub Packages feed cannot be unpublished, which is why the loop will not do it. Steps: (1) confirm Directory.Build.props <Version>, plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json version and plugin/README.md's git-subdir ref all read the number you want (all three read 0.1.0; release.yml's first step refuses a mismatch before building, so a wrong guess costs nothing); (2) `git tag v0.1.0 && git push origin v0.1.0`; (3) delete the 'Not published yet' note from README.md; (4) tick. The loop then walks the README literally in a fresh empty directory - that walk IS M6's acceptance. A PAT with read:packages in the loop environment is needed for the install half.

decisions.mermaidDialectGap: OPEN, MIRKO'S, iter113 — **the JUDGEMENT is still his; the FACTS were fully measured at iter156 and the loop must not pick an option.** beautiful-mermaid 1.1.3 renders six families and nothing else.
